Introduction
This document explains the steps for resetting the cylinder holder of the CO2 fire extinguishing system of the gas unit.
The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-
Flame detector | Heat detector | Sprinklers | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signals go from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and when the system operates or during testing, the cylinder holder is reset to the operating position.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector - and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.
